content:
infra-alert-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - Serving runtime degraded in us-west-2. Symptoms: intermittent RDMA link flaps between nodes in pool-gpu-3 -> IB QP timeouts, kernel rdma errors, followed by container restarts and CUDA failures. Affected service: inference-prod. Pager: @alice. Auto-created INC-2026-0412 and notified rotation.

alice: ack, on it. grabbing logs from gpu-node-23/24/25. are we seeing customer-facing errors yet?

infra-alert-bot: Incident INC-2026-0412 created at 2026-04-12T02:47:14Z. PagerDuty for oncall team notified.

alice: dmesg on gpu-node-23 shows repeated: "mlx5_core 0000:05:00.0: IB QP 0x... timed out" and "rdma_cm: timed out waiting for event". Container logs show intermittent "CUDA error: cuCtxSynchronize() failed" and sometimes OOM killer invoked for worker process. collecting traces now.

bob: i'm joining. based on prior incidents this smells like IB switch flaps -> RDMA stack unstable -> some long-running GPU kernels hit unexpected errors and then crash containers (kubelet restarts). immediate mitigation idea: shift traffic off this pool and route to TCP-encap fallback pool, reduce batch sizes. can someone trigger partial traffic shift? @deploy-bot?

deploy-bot: Rolling traffic changes: shifting 30% of inference-prod traffic to fallback-tcp-pool as canary. Will report success/fail.

carol: from observability: error rate for inference-prod was 0.9% -> 34% in the last 15m. p50 latency increased from 120ms -> 520ms. Tenants impacted (by request failures): acme-corp (60% errors), zebra-ads (28%), internal-evals (10%). Total failing requests ~12k in last 10m. Marking customer impact: degraded for multiple customers, some timeouts.

alice: I tried restarting rdma service (systemctl restart rdma) on node-23 which temporarily reduced QP timeouts but flaps returned after ~3m. cordoned gpu-node-23 & gpu-node-24 and started draining: kubectl drain node/gpu-node-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data. pods moved but a few restarted with CUDA errors.

netops-bot: Observed interface errors on switch sw-usw2-12 ports 10/11/12 -> link down/up events correlated with timestamps of K8s restarts. Opening cloud provider ticket and requesting on-call network engineer. Ticket: CP-14682.

alice: attaching quick iperf test between gpu-node-23 and gpu-node-25:

```
# iperf3 -c gpu-node-25
Connecting to host gpu-node-25, port 5201
[  5] local gpu-node-23 port 40918 connected to 10.2.5.25 port 5201
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth       Retr
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  9.20 GBytes   7.90 Gbits/sec  124             (retransmits observed)
```

alice: retransmits and IB errors match. also seeing "mlx5_core firmware event: link down" in kernel logs.

bob: mitigation checklist: 1) shift traffic (done), 2) cordon/drain affected nodes (in progress), 3) lower batch size + disable prefix caching on clients to reduce in-flight GPU kernels, 4) if instability continues, fallback model variant (quantized CPU) for low-latency tenants.

deploy-bot: Canary switch to model v2-quantized on fallback-tcp-pool completed for 30% traffic. No immediate error spikes on that path.

carol: drafting status page update: "We are investigating intermittent network issues affecting inference-prod in us-west-2. Some requests may fail or be delayed; engineers are actively mitigating." Will wait for ops confirmation before posting.

netops-bot: cloud provider confirmed: observed flapping on top-of-rack switch due to transient port errors; they are replacing the NIC and running diagnostics. Expected ETA for hardware swap ~45m.

dave: temporary kernel tunables we tried: increased rdma retransmit timeout to reduce immediate QP timeouts (sysctl net/rdma/retran_timeout=25) and bumped driver retry_count for mlx5. This reduced quick restarts but not a full fix. Note: changes were applied to drained nodes only to avoid cluster-wide surprises.

alice: customer impact summary for bridge and ops: - total requests dropped: ~12k in 10m window - primary cause: RDMA link flaps causing QP timeouts -> some GPU kernels fail -> container restarts -> request errors/timeouts - affected pool: pool-gpu-3 (us-west-2) - mitigation: traffic shifted to fallback-tcp-pool, drained two nodes, hardware ticket opened with provider.

bob: initiating handoff to night oncall. handing off bridge to @bob. last check: fallback path stable, error rate down to 6% overall from 34%. cloud provider ETA still ~40m. next steps for night: monitor error rate, complete node replacement once provider finishes, run full soak tests of pool-gpu-3 before uncordoning.

alice: noted. leaving logs & captures in incident channel. link to bridge: https://meet.redwood/bridge/INC-2026-0412. tagging follow-ups: postmortem (owner: netops), long-term: add automatic fallback to TCP on RDMA errors.

bob: taking over. I'll keep the incident open until nodes are replaced and we see 1h of stable metrics. leaving a short runbook entry in the incident doc for next responders:
- if RDMA QP timeouts > 1% for 10m: shift traffic to fallback-tcp-pool, cordon affected nodes, open provider ticket
- if GPU kernel OOMs persist after draining: escalate to ML runtime team to reduce batch sizes/disable caching

alice: thanks. good handoff. :thumbsup:

bob: closing note at handoff: monitoring alerts configured (error-rate, p50 latency). will update status page once provider confirms hardware replacement and we uncordon nodes.

[system message] incident-bot: INC-2026-0412 severity set to P1, bridge created, Slack channel pinned."
